collected_dynamic_variables.pain_frame: worried it’s an AI scam gadget / doesn’t want garbage
collected_dynamic_variables.pain_points: Worried it’s an AI scam gadget / doesn’t want garbage, Callers hang up / missed calls, Data privacy concern (recording/spying), Customer data storage/retention concern, Concern robot voice scares customers off

transcript:
User: Yeah I saw your thing online. Honestly this smells like one of those AI scam gadgets. Convince me it's not garbage.
Agent: I hear you—there’s a lot of junk out there. The simplest way to judge if it’s “garbage” is whether it reliably catches the calls you’re currently missing and turns them into booked jobs or solid next steps… so when a call comes in and you’re busy, what happens to that caller right now?
User: They probably just hang up. But how do I know your system isn’t spying on my calls or recording them?
Agent: Got it—that’s a fair concern. Are you asking about recording the calls themselves, or about collecting/storing customer info from the conversation?
User: Both. Who hears the calls, and where does my customer data end up?
Agent: Totally fair—so by default we don’t have some random person “listening in”; access is restricted, and we can run it in a mode where calls aren’t stored as recordings, with only the minimum details kept to handle the request (and you control retention).  

Before I get specific to your setup, what kind of business are you running?
User: Ortiz Roofing in Dallas. You're telling me I can control what gets kept and for how long?
Agent: Yeah—Ortiz Roofing can control retention: what gets saved (like basic contact + job details vs recordings) and how long it’s kept, and access is limited to your team.  

Roughly how many calls a week are you guys missing or sending to voicemail in Dallas?
User: About 30 calls a week. But why should I trust your system to handle them and not mess up?
Agent: Makes sense—if it fumbles even a few roofing leads, it’s not worth it. Of those ~30 calls a week, about how many hit voicemail or go unanswered?
User: All of them. I’m on jobs, can’t get to the phone. How’s your system supposed to help with that?
Agent: Got it—so about 30 a week are going to voicemail. If you did pick up, what percentage of those callers do you think would turn into a booked inspection or job—half, 60%?
User: Maybe 40% would book. But I'm still skeptical. How do I know your system won't drive them away?
Agent: Totally fair—if it feels weird, homeowners bounce. What’s your average ticket value on a typical job—are we talking $4,000, $8,000, $12,000?
User: Average job is about $1,800. But how do I know your system won’t scare off customers with a robot voice?
Agent: Yeah, that “robot voice” fear is real. If you booked even 40% of those 30 missed calls at $1,800, that’s about **$21600 extra a week**—and that’s just one week… about **$93500/mo**—does that sound about right?
User: I can't ignore those numbers. But I need proof your system won’t mess up before I agree to anything.
Agent: Totally get that—you shouldn’t agree to anything without hearing it and seeing exactly what it does on real roofing calls. It’s a 20‑minute walkthrough with Jay where he’ll play example call flows and show how you control the voice, the questions, and what gets saved; what’s better for you for that live call this week—later today or tomorrow?
User: Alright, set it up for tomorrow then. But this better be as good as you say.
Agent: Got it—I hear you, and we’ll make sure you can judge it for yourself on that walkthrough. What time tomorrow works best for you—morning or afternoon?
User: Afternoon works better. But remember, I'm not convinced yet. This is just to see what you've got.
Agent: Makes sense—just a look is perfect. What’s your first name?
User: You don't need my name yet. Just set up the call. My number is +14695550001.
Agent: I can set it up, but I do need your first and last name for the calendar invite and the SMS confirmation—what’s your first name?
User: Fine, it's Sam Ortiz. But if I get spammed, I'm pulling out.
Agent: Got it, Sam—and totally fair, we only use your number for the one SMS confirmation and scheduling updates. Quick check: are you on Central time in Dallas?
User: Yeah, I'm on Central time here in Dallas. Just make sure that call doesn't waste my time.
Agent: Totally fair, Sam—we’ll keep it tight and practical. I can get you in tomorrow as soon as **2026-08-27T12:15:00** or **2026-08-27T13:00:00** Central time—which works?
User: Make it 1:00 PM Central. But remember, I'm still not sold on this whole thing.
Agent: Got it—no commitment, just a 20‑minute walkthrough so you can decide after you see it. So that’s **tomorrow (Aug 27) at 1:00 PM Central**, correct?
User: Yeah, that’s right. But only a walkthrough, nothing more. Let's see if it’s worth my time.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: Perfect, Sam—you’re booked for **tomorrow (Aug 27) at 1:00 PM Central** with Jay, and you’ll get an SMS text with the confirmation details so you can add it to your calendar or reschedule if you need to.  

Is there anything else I can help you with?
User: Alright, confirm it. But remember, I'm not giving anything more until I see how this works.
Agent: Thanks, Sam! You’re all set for tomorrow (Aug 27) at 1:00 PM Central, and you’ll receive an SMS text with the confirmation details so you can add it to your calendar in one click or reschedule if you need to. Really glad you called—Jay’s looking forward to it. Have a great day. Bye!
